subject: EdgeHealth procurement readiness — PO vs marketplace (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: procurement readiness / PO vs marketplace — next steps

Hi Lisa — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned across procurement/legal/security/finance:

Summary from call:
- EdgeHealth is interested in a 6–12 month pilot for patient summarization (initial scope: 3 models, ~50k tokens/month).
- Primary commercial path preference: long-term PO (standard enterprise SOW/MPA) but you’re open to marketplace card flow for an initial pilot to speed time-to-value.
- Procurement path we should plan for: legal review -> security evidence (SOC2, data handling) -> finance approval -> PO issuance.

Proposed mutual action plan (attached: Redwood-EdgeHealth-MAP-v1.xlsx):
1) Legal review kickoff (owner: EdgeHealth legal / Redwood legal) — target start: week of Aug 30.
2) Security evidence: we shared SOC2-summary.pdf today; if you need more evidence we can provide workbook and architecture diagram. Target: 1 week parallel to legal.
3) Finance decision point: PO vs card. If you choose PO, we’ll surface standard MPA + SOW for redline. If card/pilot, we can enable a marketplace SKU for 30 days and transition later.
4) PO issuance: target within 6–8 weeks from kickoff for PO path; pilot via card can be enabled within 3 business days.

Ask: please confirm the owners (legal contact, security reviewer, finance approver) and whether procurement@edgehealth.com should be added to this thread. Also confirm if you want us to provision a marketplace pilot in parallel to legal review.

Attachments: Redwood-EdgeHealth-MAP-v1.xlsx, SOC2-summary.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 15-min alignment call if that helps.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192
From: Lisa Chen <lisa@edgehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@edgehealth.com>; Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@edgehealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-23T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement readiness / PO vs marketplace — next steps

Stephanie — thanks for the clear recap. I’ve looped in procurement and Tom (finance). A few clarifications from our side:

- Owners: Legal lead is me for contracting, security reviewer is Rajiv Kumar (security@edgehealth.com), finance approver is Tom Alvarez (cc’d). Please add procurement@edgehealth.com to future LPAs.
- SOC2: we need SOC2 Type II evidence and a short description of data retention and encryption-at-rest practices. The SOC2-summary.pdf is a good start; can you also provide the architecture diagram and the SOC2 auditor contact?
- Timeline: our internal cadence typically runs 6–10 weeks for a PO (legal + security + finance). For an expedited pilot, we’re open to a marketplace card flow for an initial month, but final decision depends on finance.

Next steps from our side: procurement will review the MAP and revert with any mandatory contract language by Aug 30. I’ll also ask Rajiv to review the SOC2 summary by Aug 27.

Thanks — Lisa
Lisa Chen
Head of Legal Operations | EdgeHealth
lisa@edgehealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@edgehealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-24T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement readiness / PO vs marketplace — next steps

Lisa — appreciate the quick turnaround and for looping Rajiv and Tom in. A few suggestions from commercial to make the procurement path smoother:

- Staged approach we recommend:
  * Stage 1 (pilot): marketplace / card for first 30 days (SKU + trial credits) so your teams can validate value without waiting for PO.
  * Stage 2 (commit): MPA + SOW for enterprise terms; start legal redline while pilot runs so PO can be issued immediately after approval.

- Contract/finance items we commonly see: billing remittance details, PO number placement, and termination/exit language. If you can share your PO template we’ll pre-fill our standard MPA clauses to reduce back-and-forth.
- Commercial concessions: for trials that convert to an annual commit we can apply a pilot credit (up to $5k) to the first invoice; we’ll document that in the MAP.

We’ve attached a simple timeline inside the MAP; if procurement prefers, Redwood can initiate the DocuSign envelope as soon as legal sends redlines to reduce cycle time.

Thanks — Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@edgehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@edgehealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-25T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement readiness / PO vs marketplace — next steps

Hi Lisa / procurement team — Karthik here from Redwood legal. Quick note on process so owners have clear expectations:

What Redwood needs from EdgeHealth to start a targeted 2-week legal review:
- Redline contact and expected legal lead (Lisa confirmed).
- Any mandatory customer terms or security addenda (please highlight).

Security evidence (owner: Rajiv):
- We will provide SOC2 Type II summary and auditor contact (attached: SOC2-summary.pdf). If Rajiv needs a deeper artifacts package we can push a dedicated workbook; please tell us the preferred transmission method (SFTP / secure Drive).

If procurement wants to run a pilot in parallel we recommend enabling the marketplace SKU immediately; we’ll reserve the SKU and issue trial credits so finance can see real usage prior to PO. If the decision is PO-first, plan for a 6–8 week cycle from legal kickoff given typical redlines and finance sign-off points.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Stephanie/Ben: provision marketplace pilot SKU and send provisioning link to Tom.
2) EdgeHealth procurement: send any mandatory PO template or clauses by Aug 30.
3) Rajiv: confirm SOC2 artifact delivery preference by Aug 27.
4) Karthik (Redwood legal): once we get redline contact, we’ll begin review (target: 2 weeks).

I’ll standby for the PO template and Rajiv’s preference.

— Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
